marble.name: Comparing Decimals
marble.subject: Mathematics
marble.description: Compare two decimals to hundredths (or up to three decimal places) by reasoning about size using place-value understanding; record with >, =, <
marble.prompt: If you compares 0.45 and 0.54, can they use place value to explain which is bigger — without reaching for a calculator?

cluster.summary: Your child is discovering their first fractions — learning to recognise and name halves and quarters as equal parts of shapes, objects, and groups.

misconceptions: Longer-is-larger: judging the decimal with more digits as larger (0.45 > 0.5, 0.311 > 0.4), treating the tail as a whole number.
Shorter-is-larger (fraction-thinking): 0.4 > 0.87 because 0.4 is read as 1/4 and 0.87 as 1/87 ('sharing among fewer gives more').
Shorter-is-larger (tenths>hundredths): 0.4 > 0.87 from the over-applied partial truth that a tenth is bigger than a hundredth.
Believing annexing a zero changes value (0.7 ≠ 0.70).
Comparing digit-by-digit from the right, or comparing the fractional parts as isolated whole numbers regardless of place.
representations: Place-value chart with decimals aligned on the point
Number line (with zoom) for locating and comparing ragged decimals
Linear Arithmetic Blocks / length model where size = length
10×10 hundredths grids shaded for each decimal to compare area
Side-by-side correct vs incorrect comparison cards for discussion
authoredAnswer: 0.312 < 0.38 < 0.4 < 0.5. Reasoning by place value: 0.312 and 0.38 have 3 tenths (smaller), and 0.312 (3 tenths 1 hundredth) is less than 0.38 (3 tenths 8 hundredths); 0.4 and 0.5 have 4 and 5 tenths. 0.7 = 0.70 — seven tenths equals seventy hundredths; the trailing zero does not change the value.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Ranks 0.312 and/or 0.38 as the largest; orders by digit count rather than by tenths.
wrongAnswers.fix: Show the length model — 0.38 is shorter than 0.4 — and reason in place value: '0.38 is 3 tenths 8 hundredths, less than 4 tenths'. Use ragged decimals; name and inhibit the whole-number rule. Reteach comparison of same-length decimals first.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Picks the shorter decimal as larger and justifies with a sharing/denominator analogy.
wrongAnswers.fix: Separate decimal place value from denominator-size reasoning: 0.4 is four tenths, 0.87 is eight tenths and seven hundredths, so 0.87 is bigger; show both on the length model. Reteach decimal comparison from place value.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Correct on pure tenth-vs-hundredth cases but wrong when the hundredths total exceeds the tenths gap (0.4 vs 0.87); may also mis-order fractions by denominator.
wrongAnswers.fix: Compare place by place from the left: 0.87 has more tenths than 0.4, so it wins before hundredths matter; grids/length model make it visible. Reteach highest-place-first comparison.
Show 7 tenths = 70 hundredths on a grid and equal lengths on the line; trailing zeros fill to equal length without changing size. Reteach place-value equivalence.
